what_it_does: This paper designs a specialized chip accelerator for running large language models efficiently. Most AI accelerators are built around the same basic primitive: matrix multiplication (multiplying arrays of numbers together). But LLM inference actually involves a different mathematical operation called tensor contraction—think of it as a more flexible generalization of matrix multiplication that can work on multi-dimensional arrays. By making tensor contraction the fundamental building block instead of matrix multiplication, RNGD unlocks parallelism opportunities hidden in LLMs' mathematical structure. The hardware can also dynamically change how it's split into smaller parallel units to match different parts of the computation, adapting in real-time to get better performance and power efficiency.
